summary: FidelityManager returns its invariant-bearing config, per-entity state map, and mutable metrics on the caller-reachable manager table. The facade is not frozen and backing state is not closure-private, so a caller crossing static typing can mutate registrations/accounting/temporal state behind validated methods; for example resetting _metrics.registered after filling a capacity-1 manager permits a second registration while retained state and aggregate counts diverge.
evidence: Current main and retained PR #385 construct ManagerImpl with public config/_states/_metrics fields and return setmetatable(self, FidelityManager) without freezing the facade or moving mutable backing state behind a closure-private capability.

register() enforces maxRegisteredEntities by reading self._metrics.registered, then writes self._states and aggregate counts; caller mutation of _metrics therefore bypasses the advertised bounded registration envelope and corrupts accounting without crossing a validation boundary.
Retained PR #385 exact head 827ce0cf63ca5f322502de883beb9f43581c69f2 hardens config/input validation and transition atomicity but retains the same manager storage shape.
PR #419 exact head 1f017628bf49365663dfc2db3a30b81ba477a0a3 adds the configured capacity ceiling but is stacked on #385 and does not hide/freeze manager-owned backing state.
The prior fidelity-extra-keys finding is a separate PolicyConfig/PolicyInputs schema-closure issue; PR/issue searches did not surface a dedicated FidelityManager private-state/frozen-facade repair.
Draft PR #490 records the source-only finding and bounded follow-up; no Luau execution, Roblox Studio, viewport, contact, networking, persistence, or two-client evidence is claimed.

metadata.recommendedNext: After retained Fidelity source lineages are explicitly unlocked and reconciled, hide mutable manager backing state behind a project-owned capability boundary and freeze the public facade. Add adversarial regressions proving public mutation cannot alter registrations/counts, pending/cooldown state, transition fences, or policy config while preserving #385/#419 semantics and O(1) operations.
